media.caption: The numbering rail: a flick charges a flywheel, and the numbers coast to a stop.
Inside a project: long air between photographs, credits in a belt along the foot.
The clicked cover flies into place and leads the gallery.
Editions: eight works on one field, inquiry only.
About: the statement set in columns, the page locked to the viewport.
On a phone, one photograph at a time beside a lane of numbers you drag like a strip.

columns.text: An art-first portfolio for Emilio Tamez, a photographer in New York, where the photographs are the only spectacle and the site behaves like a printed object. Twenty-four works sit behind a single rolling column of numbers with no first or last; a flick sets it coasting like a flywheel. Opening a project doesn't feel like navigation: the photograph you click flies into place and the page rearranges around it. Fashion commissions live apart, in a darker register of the same system.

There is no database. An editor built into the site lets Emilio reorder, write and publish in three languages, each change a single Git commit; within a day of handover she had published more than thirty times.
